title: Thieves Steal Famous Renaissance Paintings in Sicily!
summary:
Imagine sneaking into a museum and stealing paintings worth millions of dollars! That's what happened in Messina, Sicily, on Saturday night. Thieves took four artworks by a famous Renaissance painter named Antonello da Messina. The paintings are worth between $81 million and $92 million—that's more money than most people will see in their whole lives!

The thieves broke into the MuMe museum while everyone was busy celebrating a holiday called Ferragosto. They somehow got past the alarms and security guards. They stole three panels from a 1473 painting called the San Gregorio Polyptych, and another painting showing the Virgin Mary and Jesus. They even took the paintings out of a super strong glass case!

The museum director, Marisa Mercurio, said she is "devastated." She said these paintings are super important to the people of Messina because Antonello da Messina was from there. Another official said, "Messina without Antonello is deprived of the very essence of the greatest artist of the European Renaissance." That means the city feels empty without its most famous artist's work.

Art experts say the thieves might have a hard time selling the paintings because they are so famous. Everyone would recognize them! Sometimes stolen art is used as a kind of secret money between criminals. Police are investigating and hoping to find the paintings soon. This theft happened just days after police in another Italian city found three stolen paintings by other famous artists like Renoir and Matisse. Let's hope they catch these art thieves too!
why_it_matters: When art is stolen, a whole town can lose a piece of its story and identity, so protecting museums is a way of protecting shared memories for the future.

Antonello da Messina was a famous painter from Messina who lived during the Renaissance, a time of amazing European art.
Ferragosto is an Italian summer holiday celebrated on August 15, when many people go on vacation or spend time with family.

WHAT: Four Renaissance artworks worth up to $92 million were stolen from the MuMe museum.
WHERE: The theft happened in Messina, Sicily.
WHY: Thieves took advantage of the Ferragosto holiday and got past alarms and security; the art is especially beloved because its painter came from Messina.
